sections.content:
Population change in Stockton-on-Tees in 2032

The population in Stockton-on-Tees is projected to increase from 200,112 people in 2022 to 203,515 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 6,410 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Stockton-on-Tees
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Stockton-on-Tees, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 4,303, with 17,254 births and 21,557 deaths in Stockton-on-Tees between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Stockton-on-Tees by 2.2%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 1,123, with 89,000 people moving to the area and 87,876 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Stockton-on-Tees by 0.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is not projected to change the population substantially, with 2,462 people moving to the area and 2,446 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 6,410, with 10,798 people moving to the area and 4,388 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Stockton-on-Tees by 3.2%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Stockton-on-Tees in 2032

The median age in Stockton-on-Tees is projected to rise from 41 years in 2022 to 44 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 22% of the population in Stockton-on-Tees are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 40 to 49 age group are set to see the largest change in Stockton-on-Tees between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Stockton-on-Tees is projected to stay the same, at around 62%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 288 to 326 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Stockton-on-Tees?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in Stockton-on-Tees between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
